Do foot creams even work? I've also tried the Vaseline and socks trick overnight and my heels are still cracked. Neither works. I'm a dermatologist and people always make this mistake. Here's why. Both pedicures and foot creams actually work against you. Every time your heels get filed, the skin grows back thicker and harder. That's why they're rough again two weeks later. And the drugstore foot creams are mostly water. Even if you lock them in with socks and Vaseline, it doesn't go deep enough to where the cracks actually start. It stays on the surface and leaves your heels greasy instead of smooth. What actually works is something with active ingredients, urea and 0% water that penetrates deep right where cracks form. That's Sakureva, a Japanese heel stick with cold pressed Sakura extract, urea and 100% active ingredients, no water. Swipe it on 30 seconds before bed, no socks, no overnight soak. And in one week, your heels will feel smooth and soft. It's $44, lasts two months. Buy one, get one right now with a 30 day money back guarantee linked below.
